newsitem.title: NORWAY: FORECAST-Saga to post record in 1996.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Saga to post record in 1996.

text.p: Pre-tax profits at Saga Petroleum ASA are expected to jump more than 65 percent in the full-year 1996 to a record 3.38 billion crowns, according to a Reuter poll of nine Norwegian and foreign analysts.
In 1995 Norway's largest listed oil company posted profits before tax of 2.02 billion crowns.
Two of the analysts recommended to buy the share, six said hold and one said sell.

The analysts said Saga's ability to replace produced reserves with new finds was the key to the company's future development. Its commitment to move into the Atlantic Margin area off Britain was important to that strategy, they said.

"They must set down their ambitions and show increasing commitment if I am to recommend a buy on the share. Then we will see more movement in the stock and it will be more interesting. Today there are only two influences -- the oil price and the dollar -- that decide the (share) price," said one analyst with a hold recommendation.
Others said that the company needed to make discoveries in areas where it had not been found before and might turn more to gas, although they noted that earnings for gas were lower then for oil.
Saga's 1996 results will not include UK-based offshore group Santa Fe, which it bought at the end of the year.
